sprint: Two-lane separation · payment webhooks must never mint affiliate identity
business_rule: Payment lane (Liquid Clips billing) and affiliate lane (user earnings via Whop) MUST NOT be coupled. Payment webhooks activate subscriptions and reconcile EXISTING affiliates. Affiliate identity minting happens ONLY via user-triggered POST /me/affiliate/enroll. LOCKED 2026-07-18 by Daniel.

findings.summary: Pre-existing second identity-mint path — Clerk user.created webhook eagerly calls _fetch_whop_affiliate (get-or-create semantics) which mints on Whop's side. Out of scope for this diff (LOCKED rule was written in response to the 802de38a payment-webhook mint, not the Clerk-signup mint) but the same conceptual class of coupling.
findings.evidence: webhooks_clerk.py:268 `aff = _fetch_whop_affiliate((user.email or '').strip().lower())` then :270 `user.whop_affiliate_id = str(aff['id'])`. _fetch_whop_affiliate at affiliate.py:113 POSTs to /affiliates on Whop with the same payload create_affiliate_identity uses. Same coupling shape as the removed webhook block, but on the identity-provisioning lane (Clerk) not the payment lane (Whop billing).
findings.suggested_fix: Follow-up sprint: rip the eager Clerk-signup mint too and let /me/affiliate/enroll be the single mint site. Scope explicitly told me not to touch webhooks_clerk.py here. Logged as P2 (out-of-scope pre-existing) to avoid scope creep.
findings.refutation: Scope constraint from Daniel's directive explicitly excludes webhooks_clerk.py. The 802de38a bug that motivated this fix was the PAYMENT webhook minting on payment.succeeded — that specific coupling is removed and covered by regression sentinel. Broader coupling audit is a separate sprint.

findings.summary: create_affiliate_identity may raise httpx.HTTPStatusError on Whop 4xx/5xx (response.raise_for_status() at services/affiliate_commission.py:259) — that would surface as a bare FastAPI 500 to the desktop caller rather than a typed error payload.
findings.evidence: affiliate_enroll.py:79 `resp = create_affiliate_identity(user)` — no try/except. affiliate_commission.py:259 `response.raise_for_status()` inside create_affiliate_identity — httpx.HTTPStatusError bubbles up. Desktop client would see HTTP 500 body 'Internal Server Error' rather than {code: 'whop_upstream_error', ...}.
findings.reproduce: Monkeypatch httpx.Client.post to return a 500 response, call POST /me/affiliate/enroll with a paying user, observe 500 rather than a typed 502.
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap create_affiliate_identity call in try/except httpx.HTTPStatusError → raise HTTPException(502, {'code':'whop_upstream_error','message':'Please try again.'}). Skipped for this sprint per scope — user's spec only required the malformed-response 502.
findings.refutation: Spec explicitly lists the 6 required tests; upstream Whop-HTTP-error handling is not one. The malformed-id 502 IS covered (test_enroll_endpoint_handles_whop_missing_id). Upstream 5xx path fails safe (no state persisted, no override created) — user retries. Log for next iteration but not blocking.
